title: Compare strengths and limits

blocks.heading: Compare strengths and limits
blocks.text: Community-rooted learning can offer relevance and participation, while institutional education can offer broader curriculum and recognised qualifications. Either may exclude people or miss useful knowledge. Compare suitability for the learner’s goal, access and quality rather than assuming one wholly replaces the other.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Apply the distinction
blocks.text: Describe the fictional alternatives and give a reasoned judgement for a learner needing a recognised technical qualification: local demonstrations offer relevant experience but no qualification; a reachable funded course offers practice and the required qualification. The course better matches the stated goal because access and practical provision accompany recognition. Demonstrations can add relevant experience but do not supply the required qualification; they may complement the course.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect the ideas
blocks.text: Connect to Health (7.2), modern roles (6.2) and Development (1.1). Separate access, participation and learning outcomes; do not assume a system label or device purchase establishes quality.
